title: AMD has reportedly already raised GDDR6 prices for its graphics card partners, so you'll find no solace from spiking GPU prices with Team Red
summary: Getting worse before it gets better.
body: We all know RAM and SSD prices have been significantly impacted by the memory supply crisis. But it's easy for some to forget just how much dedicated memory modern graphics cards rock these days. And when I say 'some' I mean those not still trying to hunt down a reasonably priced Nvidia RTX 5090. Alas, it sounds like the broader situation shows no signs of improvement. Unfortunately for its Add-in Board partners, AMD has reportedly raised its prices for the GDDR6 memory that comes with its GPUs. According to sources on Chinese forum Boardchannels, the price increase took effect October 1 (via Benchlife ). If AIBs are having to pay more for AMD GPUs, they'll likely also raise their prices and pass the expense on to the consumer. Long story short, PC gamers will likely have to spend more on team red's wares in the near future. We've been actively monitoring graphics card prices for some time now , and sadly this is far from an unusual development. Back in July, Nvidia made a similar move with the pricing of its GDDR6 and GDDR7 cards . Reports followed that Nvidia graphics card prices were rumoured to increase by as much as 30% . title: Behold, the $3,000 keyboard that is also actually a powerful AI PC I would hate to spill my coffee on
summary: I'll be saving my pennies for something—anything—else, personally.
body: As you may already suspect, the ZX Spectrum was a bit before my time. Still, a whole home computer crammed inside a relatively svelte keyboard is something with timeless appeal. Enter HP's latest update to the EliteBoard, a modern day keyboard-PC costing far more than the ZX Spectrum ever did. HP's Eliteboard series debuted with the G1a at CES 2026 , which boasted a Kraken Point APU and a Radeon 860M integrated GPU (this made it roughly as powerful as the Steam Deck ). Already the company has come out with a refresh in the form of the HP EliteBoard G2a, which is pitched as a 'Next Gen AI PC' complete with a Copilot key. This follow-up sequesters some serious hardware inside its svelte frame for AI-geared workloads. Within what I must admit just looks like a regular office keyboard, there is up to 32 GB of RAM and an AMD Gorgon Point CPU. Pricing starts at $3,028 , with the most 'basic' model available in the US featuring 16 GB of RAM and an AMD Ryzen AI 5 Pro 435 processor. You can also only plug it into a monitor that supports a USB-C connection. title: Don't neglect crafting furniture in your Arc Raiders outpost—it unlocks hundreds of extra storage slots
summary: Turns out decorating your home away from home isn't purely cosmetic.
body: Arc Raiders ' new outpost system arrived with the Frozen Trail update, and like many I'm sure, I pretty much ignored the entire furniture aspect of it. My mind was occupied with upgrading the outpost itself, building rooms, and trying to get an Emperor Modulator and Frigate Inductor to level my Gunsmith and Research Bench. I wanted those spicy new amplified weapon upgrades like explosive bullets or incendiary shells. I assumed the whole building outpost furniture thing was a cosmetic feature, but I was dead wrong. Crafting furniture in your Arc Raiders outpost actually gives you hundreds of extra storage slots for items and weapons and it's fairly easy to unlock, you just need to: Reach level 18 to start the Sheltered Retreat project. Take a picture of the Ruined Homestead . Donate some materials including planks and sheet metal . Damage flying arc and a Bully for the final step. After that, you can complete the project and move in, recycle all of the boxes under blankets to get some planks, and start crafting some furniture. title: Gigabyte deletes blog post on Intel LGA1700 chips in early 2027, but it can't put the cat back in the bag
summary: Looks like Gigabyte made an error when it posted about Intel's upcoming LGA1700 chips last week.
body: Last week, Gigabyte suggested Intel was working on a new wave of LGA1700 processors —likely a Raptor Lake refresh for expanded DDR4 support during these memory-constrained times. It has even been busy releasing BIOS files for B760 and H610 motherboards to ensure full compatibility once those chips arrive, which it expected was around "early 2027". This week, Gigabyte has scrubbed all mention of those forthcoming chips, removed the blog post, and replaced it with another that's much less explicit. Here's the important bit from Gigabyte's blog post last week: "Built on socket LGA1700 and expected to launch in early 2027, the new processors bring fresh performance to an established platform, and Gigabyte users can be ready from day one." That's now been deleted . Gigabyte posted a new blog post on October 13 on the same topic. It notes that Gigabyte has expanded LGA1700 processor support across Z790, B760, and H610 motherboards—adding Z790 chipsets to the list. Notably, this one lacks any explicit mention of upcoming Intel chips: "[Gigabyte] today announced a new BIOS update that delivers more comprehensive LGA1700 processor support across its entire lineup of Intel Z790, B760 and H6…

title: 'Our humble goal is to survive the AI revolution' says Epic Games CEO, as its Star Wars and Marvel crossover pivots to 'AI first' development

body: An unannounced Star Wars and Marvel shooter in the works at Epic Games has been delayed, and its creators instructed to take an "AI first" approach to development. Staff were advised of the pivot last week, according to a Bloomberg report, with the project delayed indefinitely from its (unannounced) March 2027 release. That "AI first" approach seems pretty comprehensive: the instructions per Bloomberg are to "implement an 'AI first' production model using tools such as Anthropic's Claude". Art will be "generated with full AI workflows", according to the same set of instructions. Shortly after Bloomberg's report was published, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney took to X to share his own thoughts: On AI use at Epic Games in general: "We have a huge pivot underway here at Epic, moving developers around to retool for maximum AI acceleration," he said. title: People are being robbed of crypto by a tiny chip implanted in their hardware, with $100 million said to have been stolen already
summary: Investigation of the "draining incident of Oct 9th" is ongoing.
body: I never got into crypto, but when I was considering doing so I was pretty quickly convinced that I should use a hardware wallet to store my private keys, as these are usually considered to pose less of a risk of being hacked and stolen than storing everything online. But alas, it seems one of the most reputable hardware wallets on the market has fallen victim of a supply chain attack (via a reseller) that's reportedly left some users short of a tidy collective sum of at least $86 million and, according to YFarmX's calculations, potentially over $100 million . Ledger, the hardware wallet maker in question, has since said that as part of its investigation into the reports of stolen crypto, it can indeed confirm that "one of the impacted users' devices contained an unauthorised hardware implant." The company also says , "To date, all confirmed cases related to the disclosed draining incident of Oct 9th, 2026, involve devices sold through the Southeast Asia reseller CryptoBilis." Ledger says CryptoBillis confirms it has ceased all sales of the wallet until the ongoing investigation is concluded. The company also says it is "working with the appropriate authorities to bring the bad act…

title: How to turn off your backpack light in Arc Raiders
summary: Use the new feature to get real sneaky.
body: You're looking for the "Emissive" option (Image credit: Embark Studios) Key deets 💡 Arc Raiders now has an option to turn off the light on your backpack. 💡 This is the "Emissive" toggle in each backpack's cosmetic menu. Arc Raiders has made lots of new tweaks and additions with Frozen Trail's 2.0 update, but one long-requested change of significant note is that you can turn off the light on your backpacks. To do this, you need to: Select the "Raider" menu. Enter "Customization" on the bottom left of the screen. Go to the "Style" menu at the top. Choose "Backpack" on the left side. Toggle the Emissive option to "off". As you'll see, while looking at the backpack, the light will disappear and reappear as you toggle this, though where exactly the light is varies from pack to pack. This should help you be a little sneakier, though it might make your character a bit harder to spot in some of the game's darkest areas. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together

title: Arc Raiders 2.0 is here, and you can finally turn those lights on your backpack off
summary: Just because I'm sneaking around doesn't mean I don't want to look my best.
body: I remember being a kid and wishing I had shoes that lit up. I know now that I was a fool. If I festooned myself with garish lights, how would I scavenge for supplies in a frozen wasteland without being spotted by strangers who may or may not kill me before I can use my grappling hook to get away? This isn't a real problem I have, nor is it a real problem Arc Raiders players will have anymore, since your backpack now has an emissive toggle. That's one of many little overhauls that arrived in Embark Studios' popular extraction shooter Thursday, and you can read all about the rest in the 2.0 patch notes . If you've not been tuned into the extraction world as of late, you did indeed read that right: Arc Raiders has gotten a big shakeup with the Frozen Trails update , which comes bearing snowy mountains and grappling hooks. But that's not what's exciting about patch notes—the best part of combing through each little bullet point is seeing all those long-awaited bug fixes and little quality-of-life changes like the aforementioned emissive toggle for backpacks. title: The developer of an AI-powered driving instruction simulator is spending $1,000 per day just to keep its demo running
summary: Teach My Little Sister How to Drive centres around a costly chatbot.
body: One of the many ways AI will (supposedly) revolutionise the games industry is facilitating highly reactive NPCs via LLM-powered chatbots. Yet so far, only a handful of games like Where Winds Meet have attempted to implement the tech, and the results have been less than spectacular. But there might also be another reason why relatively few games feature LLM-powered NPCs, which is that powering such chatbots can be costly, as recently demonstrated by the developers of an upcoming driving instructor simulator As reported by FRVR (via Kotaku ) Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is a comic simulation game in which you coach your virtual sibling on driving technique from the comfort of the passenger seat. The twist is that behind your sister's dinner-plate eyes is an LLM chatbot (currently powered by an OpenAI model, though the developers intend to use Gemini for the final release) In the role of instructor, players can both converse with the chatbot and issue vocal instructions such as "turn left here", to which the bot will respond accordingly. At least, that's the theory. Developer Easy Fox released a demo for Teach My Little Sister How To Drive back in February, but in the past mon…

title: Squadron 42 has a Steam page
summary: Star Citizen's singleplayer mode gets a new trailer and more signs of life.
body: In August, game director Chris Roberts said that Star Citizen's singleplayer component, Squadron 42, was being delayed out of 2026 to avoid clashing with Grand Theft Auto 6 . There was a certain amount of skepticism about the reason for the delay, thanks in part to a recent Star Citizen livestream being declared a disaster , but also because, well. These games have had so many release dates the changes have their own wiki page . There's something concrete about having Squadron 42 getting a Steam page though, with system requirements and everything. Those system requirements are charmingly old-fashioned, with no mention of ray tracing-capable GPUs or DirectX 12. Although the install size of 150GB is still pretty hefty. ( Final Fantasy 7 Revelation is apparently going to be 200GB , oof.) There's also a new trailer, which leans heavily on the oorah stuff that's always a bit of a turn-off in military science-fiction. Privateer was my favorite Wing Commander game because it left out all the Top Gun nonsense, but of course it's front-and-center in Squadron 42. So too are the celebrity actors, with appearances by Mark Hamill, Gary Oldman, Rhona Mitra, that guy who played the Onion Knight…

title: WoW: Forever, by casting off modern convenience, has horseshoed back around to being casual friendly again
summary: No Season-ing.
body: Terminally Online (Image credit: Future) This is Terminally Online : PC Gamer's very own MMO column. Every other week, I'll be sharing my thoughts on the genre, interviewing fellow MMO-heads like me, taking a deep-dive into mechanics we've all taken for granted, and, occasionally, bringing in guest writers to talk about their MMO of choice. World of Warcraft: Forever seems, at first blush, like an antidote to the idea of a modern MMO. I see it in the (naturally, traditionally) insufferable trade chat as I potter about on my fury warrior—people turning up their noses at the idea of retail players. Cushioned as they are in their soft little bubbles, ptooie! But as someone with a 9-5 job and other MMOs I play, I wouldn't particularly describe myself as a "hardcore" WoW player. Competent, sure. But I'm definitely not on that grindset, particularly not in a beta. title: Triple-A Minesweeper is a gleeful send-up of blockbuster gaming's worst habits, from yellow paint to characters who talk too much
summary: "Oof, a mine!"
body: In recent years, triple-A games have often been criticised for overly excessive handholding, overcompensating for a dread fear that the player might become stuck. This has manifested in numerous ways like Atreus' heavy-handed puzzle hints in God of War: Ragnarok , yellow paint splashed on every other ledge of Stellar Blade , and most recently, Marvel's Wolverine essentially playing itself for entire portions of the game. I'm not here to weigh in on that debate. Instead, I'm simply going to point you to Triple-A Minesweeper , a delightful spoof game created by developer Mike Lacher, which expertly skewers some of blockbuster gaming's most egregious habits. Now, before I describe the experience of playing Triple-A Minesweeper, I strongly suggest that you go and play it . It only takes about five minutes, so in explaining it I will probably tell you about most of the game. It should also give you a giggle, perhaps several, even! But if you insist on reading on, then unlike regular Minesweeper, which begins by letting you play Minesweeper, Triple-A Minesweeper opens with a bunch of un-skippable title cards for third-party software and developers, before we get the dramatic title of th…

title: 'If you're skilful enough, you can chop the head off a monster, kick it midair, and then kill another monster with it': Consider me sold on this indie first-person ARPG
summary: Heathen puts a new perspective on Diablo, and it looks brilliant.
body: Certain ideas that crop up every so often in games will always grab my attention. One of them is letting players defeat enemies with bits of other enemies. As such, my interest in Heathen—an upcoming indie dungeon crawler—went from 'mildly curious' to 'smashing the wishlist button' when its most recent trailer revealed you can beat your foes by volleying other enemy heads at them. Developed by solo developer Christoper Yabsley, Heathen takes the frantic monster bashing and loot hoarding of Diablo and reworks it for a first-person perspective. Set in the fantasy town of Saltgrave, it sees your character seeking fortune and glory in the vast subterranean labyrinth beneath the town, encountering an "ancient horror" in the process in what the Steam page describes as a "descent into madness." The chief addition that the trailer explores is a new enemy dismemberment system added by Yabsley, which he says has "done a lot for making swords and axes feel really good". As a longtime fan of first-person melee games like Dark Messiah of Might and Magic and Warhammer: Vermintide 2 (the latter of which is an influence on Heathen's combat), I'm highly impressed by how slick and tactile Heathen's…
